q: Griffiths-Niu's Fig. 2 assumes ideal projective measurements with zero delay before the classical signal reaches the next box. On real hardware the mid-circuit measurement latency is ~1 microsecond and the remaining qubits decohere during that window. What is the threshold ratio (single-qubit T2) / (mid-circuit measurement + classical-routing latency) at which the semiclassical QFT starts to LOSE fidelity relative to the standard QFT, when we simulate this by inserting per-qubit depolarizing / T2 dephasing during the classical-feed-forward window?
basis: Our Aer replication used an ideal simulator with zero-latency if_test blocks, which trivially matches the standard QFT. On real IBM/Quantinuum hardware the tradeoff is a race between eliminating 2q-gate error (favors semiclassical) and adding measurement-induced idle dephasing (disfavors semiclassical). The paper predates real dynamic-circuit hardware and so cannot answer this.
next_steps: Add a NoiseModel to Aer with realistic (T1, T2, meas_time, cp_gate_time, cp_gate_error) drawn from a current IBM heron / Quantinuum H2 device sheet. Sweep meas_time in [0.1us .. 10us] and compare fidelity(semi) vs fidelity(full) for n in {4,6,8,10}. Report the crossover latency below which semiclassical wins.

q: In the periodic-input tests (n=4, p=8) our semiclassical result showed the largest full-vs-semi TVD (0.011) of any case, roughly 3x larger than the p=2 case even at the same shot budget. Is this genuinely due to more phase-corrections propagating farther (compounding shot-noise-driven correlation between measurement outcomes and later phases), or an artifact of our transpiler unroll of the if_test blocks? Formalise: does the semiclassical variant have STRICTLY higher shot-noise variance than the standard variant on any output distribution, or is the variance identical?
basis: We observed a real, small but reproducible increase in TVD(full|semi) with more Fourier peaks. In an ideal simulator the two protocols must have identical shot-noise properties (they are unitarily equivalent by the paper's argument), so any excess variance points at either (a) a transpile artifact or (b) something Griffiths-Niu did not address about shot-noise correlation structure.
next_steps: Analytically derive the joint distribution of the n classical outcomes for both protocols and prove they are equal as measures (paper does this for marginals only). Then repeat the periodic-input sweep at 10x shots (shots=163840) and check if TVD converges to 0 at the O(1/sqrt(N)) rate expected for identical distributions.

q: Griffiths-Niu eliminate every two-qubit gate in the QFT ONLY when the QFT is followed immediately by a measurement of every qubit. In a hypothetical algorithm that uses the post-QFT state as an intermediate coherent state (e.g. amplitude estimation without terminal measurement) the substitution does not apply. Is there a HYBRID variant in which one measures only the first m<n qubits semiclassically (converting m(n-m) two-qubit gates into classically-conditioned single-qubit gates), leaving the remaining coherent register live for downstream quantum operations? What is the fidelity/gate-count Pareto front over m?
basis: Both our variants terminate in measurement, matching the paper's assumption. But the paper explicitly notes the semiclassical trick works because measurement is terminal, and a natural extension is 'how far can we push it in non-terminal settings'. This came up when thinking about how modern QSVT / amplitude-estimation stacks reuse QFT sub-blocks.
next_steps: Implement a parameterised 'partially semiclassical QFT' with a knob m in {0..n}. For m=0 recover standard QFT, for m=n recover Griffiths-Niu. Study the coherent state emerging on the top n-m qubits and quantify (via state fidelity to the ideal QFT state on those qubits) the coherence cost of each additional early measurement.

q: The paper's argument for equivalence uses the consistent-histories formalism. What operational (POVM / channel) proof most directly shows equivalence WITHOUT invoking consistent histories --- i.e. can we write a completely-positive trace-preserving (CPTP) channel identity of the form (measure ~ apply classical-controlled unitary) ~ (apply CU ~ measure) as a single equation over the space of n-qubit density operators, and check it circuit-by-circuit in a way that a non-specialist reader can verify?
basis: The consistent-histories framing (Sec. 4/5 of the paper) is elegant but has been criticised as unnecessary. Our replication verified empirical equivalence but did not touch the interpretive layer. A modern channel-identity proof would make the result more portable to circuit-QED / dynamic-circuit engineers who do not know consistent-histories notation.
next_steps: Write out the exact Kraus operators for both 'CP then measure' and 'measure then classical-controlled P' on the two-qubit reduction, verify the total channels are equal element-wise, then induct across the QFT block. Publish the derivation as an appendix to the reproduction.

q: On real hardware WITHOUT dynamic-circuit support (e.g. older IBM devices before the runtime primitives release, or any hardware that only supports 'measure at the end' without feed-forward), Griffiths-Niu's substitution CANNOT be executed directly --- but 'principle of deferred measurement' says the semiclassical variant can be COMPILED into a coherent variant identical to the original standard QFT. Question: are there any circuit-transformation identities between the standard and semiclassical variant that give SHORTER total depth on a nearest-neighbour connectivity graph even after deferred-measurement reintroduces the two-qubit gates?
basis: Our replication treated dynamic circuits as first-class, but a big chunk of the field cannot use if_test yet. If deferred-measurement always yields back the original standard QFT then the semiclassical protocol brings no benefit on those platforms. But the paper's counting suggests every CP gate becomes a P gate + a CNOT under deferred measurement, and on a linear-nearest-neighbour graph those may route differently.
next_steps: Take our semiclassical circuit, run Qiskit's 'defer_measurements' pass, then transpile both the deferred-semiclassical and the original standard-QFT circuits onto a linear-nearest-neighbour coupling map at n=10..20 and compare CNOT count and depth. If the deferred-semiclassical is strictly no better, quantify the 'dynamic-circuits premium' as an argument for adding if_test support to more hardware.
